problem: always #5 clk = ~clk; does not give a 10 ns period on its own. A reg starts as x, and ~x is still x, so the clock line stays x forever and every clocked block in the bench stalls. The delay unit also depends on the timescale directive, not on ns by default.
fix: Show the full idiom: `timescale 1ns/1ps then reg clk = 0; (or initial clk = 0;) followed by always #5 clk = ~clk;. With a 1 ns/1 ps timescale, #5 is 5 ns, so the period is 10 ns.

problem: "For clocked logic, sample after the setup time has passed" is wrong: setup time is a constraint on the input before the active clock edge, not a delay after it. Sampling is timed from the edge, after the flip-flop's clock-to-Q delay.
fix: For clocked logic, sample a short delay after the active edge (for example y sampled #1 after posedge clk), so the clock-to-Q delay has passed. Setup and hold times are checked on the DUT inputs relative to the edge, not on when the bench samples.

problem: It says "The checker drives each vector, waits #10 ... then compares", which mixes the stimulus role and the checker role and can confuse students writing the two blocks.
fix: The initial (stimulus) block drives each vector; after #10 the checker compares y with the expected value, increments errors on a mismatch, and PASS is printed only when errors=0.
